report:
**Conclusion: Yes.** In postmenopausal women with osteoporosis, denosumab (Prolia) 60 mg subcutaneously every 6 months substantially reduces vertebral fracture risk.

The pivotal FREEDOM trial (7,868 women, randomized, placebo-controlled, 3 years) found new radiographic vertebral fractures in 2.3% on denosumab vs 7.2% on placebo (risk ratio 0.32; 95% CI 0.26–0.41; P<0.001), a 68% relative reduction; hip and nonvertebral fractures also fell. Regulatory labeling reflects this: FDA states Prolia treats postmenopausal osteoporosis at high fracture risk and reduces vertebral, nonvertebral, and hip fracture incidence. Systematic reviews are consistent.

Important caveat: protection is not permanent. After discontinuation, vertebral fracture rates rise back toward untreated levels and multiple vertebral fractures have been reported, so stopping should be paired with follow-on antiresorptive therapy and clinician supervision. Ensure adequate calcium/vitamin D and discuss hypocalcemia, infection, osteonecrosis of the jaw, and atypical femoral fracture risks.
